difficulty_reason: The theorem collects the fundamental properties of the plus construction: it is separated, it is a sheaf with injective canonical map when the presheaf is separated, the canonical map is an isomorphism for sheaves, and iterating it once more always gives a sheaf (statement lines 2191-2210). The proof is a complete argument: separatedness is obtained by choosing presentations of the two elements and a common refinement and using the separatedness of the presheaf (proof lines 2213-2227); the sheaf property and injectivity are proved by choosing local representatives of a compatible family, checking compatibility on the pairwise products and amalgamating in the plus construction, with the author leaving to the reader only the final restriction check (proof lines 2230-2249); and the last two statements follow directly from the definitions (proof lines 2252-2258). The non-formal content is the two constructions and the amalgamation. The claim is H2: the parts are written out with each input named.
